# @gamebyte/gamelabsjs

TypeScript skeleton + reusable modules for web games. Three.js (3D world) + PixiJS (2D HUD/UI) + GSAP (animations). Designed for AI-generated game projects with human review.

## Core concepts

- `GamelabsApp`: base app class. Extend it, override lifecycle methods.
- Two DI containers: `diContainer` (controllers/utilities/events), `viewDiContainer` (views).
- View/Controller separation: views render + handle input, controllers own behavior + state.
- Two view layers: World (Three.js, `WorldViewBase`), Hud (PixiJS, `HudViewBase`, `ScreenView`).
- Modules: reusable feature bundles via `ModuleBinding` (DI + views + assets).
- Events: `Set<cb>` + `Unsubscribe` pattern, cleanup with `UnsubscribeBag`.
- InjectionToken pattern: `export const IFoo = new InjectionToken<IFoo>("IFoo")`.

## App lifecycle (in order)

1. `registerModules()` — `addModule(binding)`
2. `configureDI()` — bind to DI containers
3. `configureViews()` — `viewFactory.register<View, Controller>(View, Controller)`
4. `loadAssets()` — `assetManager.load(type, id, url)`
5. `postInitialize()` — create screens/views, subscribe events (assets loaded)
6. `onStep(dt)` — per-frame hook
7. `preDestroy()` — cleanup

## Viewport / aspect fit

Portrait or fixed-aspect games: set `viewport` in the app config so the play area never stretches to fill the window. `new MyApp({ mount, viewport: { fit: "contain", minAspect: 9 / 19.5, maxAspect: 9 / 16, background: "#0f172a" } })` letterboxes/pillarboxes both canvases to the clamped aspect; the bars are inert (pointer input ignored) and cameras/HUD/DPR all follow the play-rect — no per-view code. A single `aspectRatio` locks one exact aspect. Omit `viewport` (or use `fit: "fill"`) to fill the mount (default, unchanged).

## File naming

- `IFoo.ts` (interfaces), `FooView.pixi.ts` (HUD), `FooView.three.ts` (world), `FooViewController.ts` (every controller is a view controller — the suffix stays explicit), `FooEvents.ts`
- Asset IDs: enum with namespaced values `"MyGame.ItemName"`
- Every per-board gamegrid class an example defines uses role-based `GameBoard*` prefix (not game prefix): `GameBoardItem`, `IGameBoardsView`, `GameBoardsView`, `GameBoardsViewController`, `GameBoardCellObject`, `GameBoardItemObject`, `GameBoardItemObjectOptions`, `GameBoardObjectCreator`. App / Config / AssetIds / Events / Service / Binding / screen views keep the game prefix.

## Project layout

`controllers/`, `events/`, `models/`, `utilities/`, `views/` + `MyGameApp.ts`, `MyGameAssetIds.ts`, `MyGameConfig.ts`

## Rules

- Views must NOT access `diContainer`. Controllers must NOT touch rendering objects.
- Controllers reference view interfaces (`IMyView`), not concrete classes.
- Cross-feature communication through event classes only. No direct controller-to-controller calls.
- Scene setup (fog, lights) belongs in views, not app class.
- Game objects render either in a World view (`*View.three.ts`, `world.addView`) — for 3D or World-only tools (gamecamera, 3D particles, lighting) — or in a HUD Content-layer Pixi view (`*View.pixi.ts`, `hud.addChild(HudLayer.Content, view)`) for pure-2D games using Pixi's 2D stack. Choose by the tools needed, not dimensionality. UI/chrome is always a separate Screen-layer view (`ScreenView`); never put gameplay objects in the UI screen view.
- Event classes use `Set<cb>` + `Unsubscribe`. Use `UnsubscribeBag` for cleanup.
- No empty lifecycle overrides. Only override when adding behavior.
- Modules must not depend on app-specific code.

## Where logic lives

Three buckets — pick before writing a class:

- **Domain rules / operations** → `utilities/`, suffix `*Operations` / `*Rules` / `*Solver`. Pure in-app logic on models. No DOM, no network, no browser APIs. Unit-testable without a view. Examples: `GameOperations` (the per-game operations class in match3 and 2048), `WaterSortOperations`, match-finders, move solvers.
- **State managers** → `utilities/`, suffix `*Manager`. Own mutable subsystem state across controller methods. Examples: `TurnManager`, `WaveManager`, `UpdateManager`, `SettingsManager`.
- **Services** → `services/`, suffix `*Service`. Boundaries to the outside world — anything that can fail because of the environment (network, quota, permission, autoplay). Examples: `StorageService`, `AudioService`, `NotificationService`, `*ApiService`. **Do not use `*Service` for in-app logic.**

Controllers stay thin: sequence async work, branch on results, dispatch events. Extract computation into `*Operations` / `*Rules` / `*Manager` classes in `utilities/` when it would be unit-testable without a view.

## Built-in modules

uicomponents (Button/Background/Image/layout/list/scrollview/dropdown/toggle/slider/label), gamecamera (camera controllers + named-channel offsets + follow/constraint strategies + cinematic tracks), gamegrid (grid system), mainscreen (main menu), levelprogressscreen (level select), onscreencontrols (virtual joystick/buttons), settings (manager + popup UI), audiodsp (filter/reverb/delay/distortion/compressor), timeline (time-bounded Track lifecycle for effects), particles (THREE + Pixi emitters with global budget).

## Optional physics modules (subpath imports)

Imported from their own subpaths, NOT the main entry — so non-physics games never load the engines. Engines are optional peer deps (`matter-js` / `cannon-es`).

- `@gamebyte/gamelabsjs/physics2d` — `Physics2DManager` (matter-js, 2D). `Physics2DBinding`, `Physics2DSyncBag`, `Physics2DStage`, `FakePhysics2D`.
- `@gamebyte/gamelabsjs/physics3d` — `Physics3DManager` (cannon-es, 3D). `Physics3DBinding`, `Physics3DSyncBag`, `Physics3DStage`, `FakePhysics3D`.

Axis is dimension, not renderer (a 3D game with a Pixi HUD still uses physics3d). Both follow the standard module pattern: `addModule(new PhysicsXDBinding(config))` in `registerModules()`, then resolve the manager in `postInitialize()` and `updateManager.register((dt) => manager.step(dt), -1000)` so physics steps before gameplay controllers.

**Boundary rule (enforce in generated code):** physics is a state producer behind the manager — it is NOT view-side. Bodies are created by controllers/utilities, never by views; a view never imports a physics manager or reads the physics world. Data flow is one-way: manager → controller → view. Transforms are PULLED (controller reads `getTransform`, pushes to the view via `PhysicsXDSyncBag`); collisions are PUSHED as events carrying body ids (`onCollisionStart`/`onCollisionEnd`) — the controller maps ids (or `getTag(id)`) to gameplay and decides. Engine types (`Matter.*` / `CANNON.*`) never cross the manager API. Bodies: `dynamic`/`static`/`kinematic` (kinematic driven by `setKinematicTarget`, not forces). Unit-test controllers with `FakePhysics2D`/`FakePhysics3D` (no engine needed). Pair bodies with view objects via `PhysicsXDSyncBag` (bind an existing body id) or `PhysicsXDStage` (prefab-style: `spawn(body, entityView)` creates body+view+sync in one call, `despawn()`/`clear()` tear down, `sync()` per frame); the body stays in the central manager either way.

## Commands

`npm run build` (tsup), `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit). Examples: `cd examples/<name> && npm i && npm run dev`.
